deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. Each block is headed 'p. h'. The p values are 1321, 1297, 1289, 1249, 1217, 1201, 1193, 1153, 1129, 1097, 1049, 1033 and 1009. These are, in descending order, all 13 primes p ≡ 1 (mod 8) between 1009 and 1321. h is Gauss's class number of properly primitive positive binary forms (a,b,c) = ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 of determinant b^2-ac = -p. In modern terms this is h(-4p), always divisible by 4 for these p.

Each table row 'k | a.b' records a representative (a, b, (b^2+p)/a) of the class f^k, where f is the class in row 1. Gauss computes the successive powers of f by composition, followed by reduction or a change of b mod a. He stops at k = h/2, where he reaches the ambiguous form (2,1,(p+1)/2). Since f^{h/2} is the non-principal ambiguous class and the listed classes are distinct, f has order exactly h. So the class group is cyclic, generated by f, and the class number is confirmed.

EXAMPLE (my verification). For p = 1297, f = (11,1,118). Composing f with itself gives B ≡ 1 (mod 11) with B^2 ≡ -1297 (mod 121), so B = 78. This yields (121,78,61), which reduces in turn to (61,44,53), then (53,9,26), then (26,17,61). That is Gauss's row 2, '26.17'. Rows 3-6 are 31.25, 13.9, 22.21 and 2.1, so f^6 = (2,1,649) and h = 12.

For p = 1321, f = (19,3,70). Here B = 22 gives (361,22,5), equivalent to (5,3,266); this is row 2, '5.3'. Row 12 is 2.1, so h = 24.

LATE ROWS. Often only a is written. When the generator is (3,1,·), the last rows are 18, 6, 2, because f^{h/2-j} = (2,1)·f^{-j} has a = 2·3^j. With generator (7,·) the end is 14, 2, and with (11,·) it is 22.b, 2.1. The a-values never exceed about 2·sqrt(p/3) (with exceptions such as 41 for 1153 and 1321), but b is recorded as a residue mod a, not always reduced.

Every listed pair satisfies a | b^2+p; all were checked. Two tables are not finished:
- 1097: rows 16-18 are blank.
- 1249: the bottom rows are crossed out and rewritten.

SIDE CALCULATIONS.
(a) Columns 1 and 2 contain a frequency tally written as 'count.value product':
- 12·6=72, 3·7=21, 12·8=96, 7·9=63, 5·10=50, giving a count of 39 and a value-sum of 302;
- 2·1, 2·2, 4·3, 8·4, 2·5, giving 18 and 60;
- 4·12, 3·13, 1·14, 1·15, 1·16, giving 10 and 132.
The grand totals are 67 items and 494. This is a distribution of some quantity taking values 1..16; plausibly h/4 over a range of primes, but that is unsure.
(b) Beside 1049 there is a separate exercise in determinant -2938 = -2·13·113. It lists the ambiguous forms (1,0,2938), (2,0,1469), (13,0,226) and (26,0,113), and computes powers of (7,3,421): its square is (49,10,62) and its cube is (13,0,226). The text has '13.0'; the cube was checked by me, so the class has order 6.
(c) Beside 1033 (h = 12) there are representations of p as a sum of three squares: 32^2+3^2+0^2, 22^2+18^2+15^2, and 31^2+6^2+6^2 (read '31.36.36'). This matches the next page, where 2017 (h = 12) gets four triples totalling 144 = 12h representations. That is Gauss's theorem r_3(p) = 12h(-4p) for p ≡ 1 (mod 4) (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae arts. 291-292). For 1033 the triple 24^2+21^2+4^2 (48 representations) is missing: the listed triples give only 24+48+24 = 96.
(d) Bottom right: the 13 class numbers are sorted as 36 (written above) plus 44, 36, 36, 32, 32, 24, 20, 16, 16, 16, 12, 12, which sum to 332. This is added to the running total from the previous page ('18 640'), giving the cumulative '31. 972': 31 primes with sum of class numbers 972 (18+13 = 31, 640+332 = 972).

results.what: Tables of powers of a generating class for forms of determinant -p, for primes p ≡ 1 mod 8 from 1009 to 1321. Each shows the class group is cyclic of order h, reaching the ambiguous class (2,1,(p+1)/2) at f^{h/2}. Class numbers obtained: 1321:24, 1297:12, 1289:36, 1249:32, 1217:32, 1201:16, 1193:36, 1153:16, 1129:16, 1097:36, 1049:44, 1033:12, 1009:20.
results.modern_name: Structure of the form class group Cl(-4p), cyclic generator, class number h(-4p) with 4 | h for p ≡ 1 mod 8
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, arts. 303-306; class-number tables in Werke II)

results.what: Running tallies of class numbers over batches of primes (332 for 13 primes; cumulative 972 over 31 primes), as empirical data on average class numbers.
results.modern_name: Empirical average order of class numbers
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (DA art. 302, mean-value statements; proofs later by Lipschitz and Mertens)

results.what: Representations of p as sums of three squares listed next to class number h(-4p) (1033 here, 2017 on the next page), consistent with r_3(p) = 12h(-4p).
Side computation in determinant -2938: ambiguous forms and powers of (7,3,421); its cube is (13,0,226).
results.modern_name: Composition of forms / 2-torsion in class group

deep.surprise_reason: These are working tables for Gauss's well-known class-number computations: cyclic class groups, ambiguous classes and average class numbers. Together with the three-squares check of r_3 = 12h, this is material from the Disquisitiones and his published Nachlass tables. The computations are correct but contain nothing beyond what is known as his.
